en: The Path of Discrimination 3:
The Chapter on Wisdom 3.6.
The Discourse on Marvels
“Bhikkhus, there are these three wonders.
Which three?
The wonder of psychic power, the wonder of mind-reading, and the wonder of instruction.”
And what, monks, is the miracle of psychic power?
Here, monks, a certain person experiences various kinds of psychic power:
having been one, he becomes many; having been many, he becomes one.
Manifestation and disappearance...
[and so on] ...even as far as the Brahma-world, he wields mastery with his body.
This, monks, is called a miracle of psychic power.
And what, monks, is the miracle of direct communication?
Here, monks, someone communicates by means of a sign:
"Your mind is thus; your mind is so; your consciousness is such-and-such."
Thus, even if he predicts much, it happens exactly so and not otherwise.
But here, monks, a certain person does not predict by means of a sign; rather, having heard the voice of humans, non-humans, or deities, he predicts:
"Your mind is thus, your mind is such, your consciousness is such-and-such."
Thus, even if one predicts much, it happens exactly so and not otherwise.
But here, monks, a certain person does not predict by means of a sign, nor does he predict after hearing the voices of humans, non-humans, or deities;
rather, while thinking and pondering, he predicts after hearing the sound produced by the movement of thought.
‘Such is your mind, this is your mind, such is your consciousness.
Even if he predicts much, it happens exactly so and not otherwise.
But here, monks, a certain person does not predict by means of a sign, nor by means of humans or non-humans.
Nor does he announce it after hearing the sound of deities or the sound produced by the movement of thought while one is thinking and examining;
rather, having entered a concentration free from directed thought and evaluation, he understands the mind with his own mind:
"In accordance with how this venerable one’s mental formations are directed, immediately following this consciousness, such-and-such a thought will arise."
Whatever he thus predicts, even if it is much, happens exactly so and not otherwise.
This, monks, is called the miracle of direct address (*ādesanā-pāṭihāriya*).
And what, monks, is the miracle of instruction (*anusāsanī-pāṭihāriya*)?
In this case, monks, a certain person instructs thus:
"Direct your thoughts in this way; do not direct your thoughts in that way.
Attend to the mind in this way; do not attend to the mind in that way."
“Abandon this; having entered upon this, dwell therein.
This, monks, is called the miracle of instruction.
These, monks, are the three miracles.
Renunciation succeeds, thus it is *iddhi* (success).
It repels sensual desire, thus it is *pāṭihāriya* (a marvel).
Those who are endowed with that renunciation—all of them have purified minds and unturbid intentions.
The miracle of direct instruction.

And as for that renunciation: "It should be cultivated in this way, developed in this way, practiced extensively in this way, and mindfulness in accordance with its nature should be established"—this is the miracle of instruction.
Non-ill will succeeds, thus it is *iddhi*.
It repels ill will, thus it is a *pāṭihāriya*.
Those who are endowed with that non-ill will—all of them have purified minds and untroubled intentions.
The miracle of direct communication.

Furthermore, the thought: “That very non-ill will is to be cultivated in this way, developed in this way, practiced frequently in this way, and mindfulness in accordance with its nature is to be established in this way”—this is the miracle of instruction.
The perception of light succeeds, thus it is "success" (iddhi).
It wards off sloth and torpor, thus it is a "wonder" (pāṭihāriya).
Those who are endowed with that perception of light—all of them have purified minds and untroubled intentions.
The miracle of direct instruction (*ādesanā-pāṭihāriya*).

And as for that perception of light: “It should be cultivated in this way, developed in this way, made much of in this way, and mindfulness in accordance with it should be established in this way”—this is the miracle of instruction (*anusāsanī-pāṭihāriya*).
Non-distraction succeeds, thus it is *iddhi* (success).
It counteracts restlessness, thus it is *pāṭihāriya* (wonder).
All those who are endowed with that non-distraction have purified minds and untroubled intentions.
The miracle of direct instruction (*ādesanā-pāṭihāriya*).

And furthermore: “That non-distraction should be practiced in this way, developed in this way, cultivated in this way, and mindfulness in accordance with its nature should be established in this way”—this is the miracle of instruction (*anusāsanī-pāṭihāriya*).
The discernment of phenomena succeeds, thus it is *iddhi* (success).
It wards off doubt, thus it is a *pāṭihāriya* (manifestation of power).
Those who are endowed with that discernment of phenomena—all of them have purified minds and are undisturbed in their intentions.
The miracle of direct communication (*ādesanā-pāṭihāriya*).

Furthermore, the instruction: “That very discernment of phenomena (*dhamma-vavatthāna*) should be cultivated in this way, developed in this way, practiced extensively in this way; in accordance with that, mindfulness (*sati*) should be established”—this is the miracle of instruction (*anusāsanī-pāṭihāriya*).
Knowledge succeeds, thus it is *iddhi*.
It repels ignorance, thus it is a *pāṭihāriya*.
Those who are endowed with that knowledge—all of them have purified minds and are unturbid in their intentions.
The miracle of direct communication.

Furthermore, the miracle of instruction is: “That knowledge should be cultivated in this way, developed in this way, practiced frequently in this way, and mindfulness in accordance with that [knowledge] should be established in this way.”
"Delight succeeds"—this is *iddhi*.
"It wards off discontent"—this is *pāṭihāriya*.
Those who are endowed with that delight, all of them have purified minds and untroubled intentions.
The miracle of direct communication.

“Furthermore, that gladness should be cultivated in this way, developed in this way, made much of in this way, and mindfulness in accordance with it should be established in this way”—this is the miracle of instruction. …pe…
The first jhāna succeeds, thus it is *iddhi* (success).
It wards off the hindrances, thus it is a *pāṭihāriya* (wonder).
All those who are endowed with that first jhāna have purified minds and are unturbid in their intentions.
The miracle of direct communication.

Furthermore, the miracle of instruction is as follows: "That first jhāna should be cultivated in this way, developed in this way, practiced extensively in this way, and mindfulness in accordance with its nature should be established in this way.
...pe... [and so on].
The path of arahantship succeeds, thus it is *iddhi*.
It repels all defilements, thus it is a *pāṭihāriya*.
Those who are endowed with that path of arahantship are all pure-minded and have untroubled intentions.
The miracle of direct communication.

And as for this path to arahantship: "It is to be cultivated in this way, developed in this way, practiced extensively in this way, and mindfulness in accordance with it is to be established"—this is the miracle of instruction.
Renunciation succeeds, thus it is success (*iddhi*).
It repels sensual desire, thus it is a marvel (*pāṭihāriya*).
That which is success and that which is a marvel—this is called the marvel of success (*iddhipāṭihāriya*).
Non-ill will succeeds, thus it is "success" (iddhi).
It repels ill will, thus it is a "wonder" (pāṭihāriya).
That which is success and that which is a wonder—this is called the "wonder of success" (iddhipāṭihāriya).
The perception of light succeeds, thus it is *iddhi*.
It wards off sloth and torpor, thus it is a *pāṭihāriya*...
pe ...the path to arahantship succeeds, thus it is *iddhi*.
It wards off all defilements, thus it is a "miracle" (*pāṭihāriya*).
That which is psychic power (*iddhi*) and that which is a miracle—this is called the "miracle of psychic power" (*iddhipāṭihāriya*).
The Discussion on Miracles is finished.
